stories.author: SamuraiLion
stories.title: A 386 PC for Your RP2350
stories.groq_label: An RP2350 microcontroller can emulate a full 386 PC with 8MB PSRAM and HDMI output capable of booting Windows 95 and Linux.
stories.groq_explain: You can now turn an inexpensive Raspberry Pi Pico 2 microcontroller into a fully working retro 386 PC. By loading this software onto compatible hardware, you can run classic operating systems like MS-DOS, Windows 95, and old-school Linux directly from an SD card, complete with monitor output, sound, and keyboard support. It makes retro computing accessible, cheap, and tiny without needing original, fragile vintage hardware.

stories.author: NKosmatos
stories.title: EuroBirdPortal – Live bird movements across Europe
stories.groq_label: EuroBirdPortal maps real-time and seasonal bird migrations across Europe using aggregated observation data.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Short:

This project addresses the challenge of tracking and visualizing live bird movements across Europe. Hacker News commenters generally appreciated the compelling concept of visualizing migration patterns and believed the project could be an engaging resource for birdwatchers and researchers. However, they also expressed concerns about unintuitive navigation and questioned how to switch between different bird species on the site. Overall, the discussion was mixed, with commenters recognizing both the project's potential and its limitations.

stories.author: zenpe
stories.title: Show HN: 1080p is 920px tall – 1k real browser viewports
stories.groq_label: Browser chrome consumes vertical screen space on 1080p displays, leaving only about 920 pixels of usable viewport height.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Balanced:

This project aims to solve the problem of understanding real-world browser viewport dimensions. The Hacker News discussion was generally mixed, with many commenters appreciating the validation of usable viewport heights and the project's approach to measuring browser chrome impact. At the same time, several commenters raised concerns about presentation quality and data granularity, arguing that the project appears to be low-effort AI-generated content and lacks cumulative size distribution metrics. Overall, the discussion suggests that the community sees promise in the project but believes there are important challenges that still need to be addressed.

stories.author: bryanrasmussen
stories.title: Of Gods and Languages: On "When God Spoke Greek" (2013)
stories.groq_label: Early Christian canon and Eastern Orthodox traditions rely on Greek Septuagint translations rather than Hebrew texts, despite the original Septuagint containing only the Torah.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Balanced:

This article aims to solve the problem of understanding the historical and linguistic evolution of sacred scripture, specifically the role of the Greek Septuagint in biblical history. The Hacker News discussion was generally mixed, with many commenters appreciating the historical perspective on ancient texts and the project's approach to distinguishing between modern Bibles and ancient scripture. At the same time, several commenters raised concerns about historical inaccuracies and Western bias, arguing that the Septuagint originally included only the Torah and that the theological visions of the Hebrew and Greek versions are more aligned than the article suggests. Overall, the discussion suggests that the community sees promise in the project but believes there are important challenges that still need to be addressed.

stories.author: negura
stories.title: OEMpocalypse: Unprivileged Android app to root on Samsung, Xiaomi, others
stories.groq_label: Exploiting page use-after-free bugs in OEM-specific drivers allows an unprivileged app to gain root across Samsung, Xiaomi, and Oppo devices while bypassing kernel hardening.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: Short:

This blog post addresses privilege escalation vulnerabilities allowing unprivileged Android apps to gain root access on OEM devices. Hacker News commenters generally appreciated the technical exposure of OEM driver flaws and believed the research could motivate vendors to improve device security. However, they also expressed concerns about closed proprietary drivers and questioned the overall security and safety of rooting modern devices. Overall, the discussion was critical of Android OEM security, with commenters recognizing both the research's value and the concerning security implications for the platform.
stories.groq_explain: Security researchers found a way for a basic, unprivileged Android app to gain full root control over millions of Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo, and OnePlus phones. Instead of attacking core Android code, the technique targets flaws in the custom software added by the phone manufacturers themselves. This makes the hack work consistently across a massive range of devices while easily bypassing standard security protections.

stories.author: contact9879
stories.title: The case against JPEG XL
stories.groq_label: JPEG XL enables byte-exact, lossless re-compression of existing JPEGs at smaller file sizes, but its complex feature set trades web delivery efficiency for archival versatility.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Community Perspective:

The Hacker News community generally responded to this article with mixed reactions. Many commenters appreciated JPEG XL's versatility and considered it useful because it enables lossless re-encoding of existing JPEG files for free storage savings. Others highlighted its suitability for personal archives and high-resolution image pipelines as one of the project's most valuable aspects. Nevertheless, recurring criticisms focused on performance and decoder limits, particularly high CPU and memory consumption during complex decoding tasks. As a whole, commenters viewed the project as an interesting contribution while acknowledging that it still has room for improvement.
